summary: Ansible officially supports only the OpenSSH that ships with Windows, at version 7.9.0.0 or later, which effectively means Windows Server 2022 and up. A PowerShell script installs the OpenSSH server capability, starts sshd automatically, opens port 22 in the firewall and sets PowerShell as the default shell.
questions: How do I install OpenSSH server on Windows Server 2022?
Is Windows Server 2019 supported for SSH with Ansible?
What minimum OpenSSH version does Ansible need on Windows?
Is the upstream Win32-OpenSSH package supported by Ansible?
How do I open the firewall for sshd on Windows?

answer_card.title: Setting up OpenSSH on Windows for Ansible
answer_card.answer_md:
Ansible officially supports only the OpenSSH shipped with Windows (not the upstream Win32-OpenSSH package), version **7.9.0.0** or later. Server 2019 ships 7.7.2.1, so official support effectively starts with **Windows Server 2022**. Older versions or the upstream package may work but aren't supported.

Install on Server 2022+:

```powershell
Get-WindowsCapability -Name OpenSSH.Server* -Online |
    Add-WindowsCapability -Online
Set-Service -Name sshd -StartupType Automatic -Status Running

$firewallParams = @{
    Name        = 'sshd-Server-In-TCP'
    DisplayName = 'Inbound rule for OpenSSH Server (sshd) on TCP port 22'
    Action      = 'Allow'
    Direction   = 'Inbound'
    Enabled     = 'True'  # enum, not boolean
    Profile     = 'Any'
    Protocol    = 'TCP'
    LocalPort   = 22
}
New-NetFirewallRule @firewallParams

$shellParams = @{
    Path         = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\OpenSSH'
    Name         = 'DefaultShell'
    Value        = 'C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe'
    PropertyType = 'String'
    Force        = $true
}
New-ItemProperty @shellParams
```
